class.name: TerrainMaterial3D
class.brief_description: A ground material built from geology, erosion detail, grass tint, wetness and snow.
class.description: A material that writes its own shader. It picks among five [TerrainMaterialLayer]s per pixel: bare rock, scree, soil, alluvium and beach sand. With a [TerrainGenerator3D] (see [method use_generator]) the choice follows the generator's geology maps; without one, rock takes slopes past [member rock_slope] and soil the rest. Layers meet by height blending (Mishkinis 2013). Past [member cliff_slope] textures are mapped biplanar (Quilez 2020) so cliffs do not stretch. Over the layers come the generator's erosion detail normal, the [GrassField3D] ground tint, the [WeatherMap3D]'s wetness and the [SnowCover3D] snowpack, using the same shader code as [BaseMaterial3D] (see [method BaseMaterial3D.get_snow_shader_code]), so snow and wet ground look the same on the terrain as on every other surface, rasterized or path traced.

method.name: get_layer
method.description: Returns the layer for a surface, or [code]null[/code] for the default.

method.name: get_shader_code
method.description: Returns the shader code the material writes for its current settings.

method.name: set_layer
method.description: Sets the layer for a surface. [code]null[/code] uses a plain default.

method.name: update_shader
method.description: Writes the shader again. Setters that change the code call it themselves.

method.name: use_generator
method.description: Takes [member sea_level] and the erosion detail code from a [TerrainGenerator3D] that has generated. The geology maps reach the shader through the generator's global uniforms.

members.member: Log10 of the drainage area (m²) past which soil turns to alluvium.
Height above [member sea_level] that sand reaches.
Height-blend transition depth. Smaller gives sharper borders between layers.
Slope in degrees past which textures are mapped biplanar.
Shader code that defines [code]terrain_detail_normal()[/code], usually [method TerrainGenerator3D.get_detail_shader_code]. Empty: no erosion detail.
Octaves of the erosion detail normal. It fades out where a pixel covers it.
Follow the generator's geology maps when they are set.
Tint the ground where [GrassField3D] grows, as [method GrassField3D.get_ground_shader_code] does.
Slope in degrees past which rock shows, with or without geology.
Height of the sea, the base of the beach band.
Lay the [SnowCover3D] snowpack over the ground.
Slope in degrees past which snow slides off (see [member BaseMaterial3D.snow_max_slope]).
Darken and smooth the ground where the [WeatherMap3D] says it is wet, by each layer's [member TerrainMaterialLayer.porosity].
